d.flavorText: The volcanoes on its back have a major eruption every 10 years—or whenever it becomes really angry.

d.name: Litwick

attacks.name: Find a Friend

d.flavorText: While shining a light and pretending to be a guide, it leeches off the life force of any who follow it.

d.name: Litwick

attacks.name: Fireworks

d.flavorText: The spirits it absorbs fuel its baleful fire. It hangs around hospitals waiting for people to pass on.

d.name: Chandelure

d.flavorText: Being consumed in Chandelure's flame burns up the spirit, leaving the body behind.

d.name: Fletchinder

attacks.name: Flame Charge
attacks.text: Search your deck for a Fire Energy card and attach it to this Pokémon. Then, shuffle your deck.

d.flavorText: It scatters embers in the tall grass. Then bug Pokémon, frightened by the flames, come flying out, and Fletchinder gobbles them up.

d.name: Talonflame

d.flavorText: Its tough wings don't allow fire to pass through them. A long time ago, firefighters' outfits were made from Talonflame wings.

d.name: Salandit
d.flavorText: The males will do whatever the females tell them. They give the females most of their food. Due to malnutrition, the males can't evolve.

d.name: Salazzle
d.flavorText: Salazzle lives deep in caves and forces the Salandit it has attracted with its pheromones to serve it.

d.name: Lapras

abilities.name: Mermaid's Call
abilities.text: Once during your turn (before your attack), you may put a Misty's Favor card from your discard pile into your hand.

d.flavorText: It likes swimming around with people on its back. In the Alola region, it's an important means of transportation over water.

d.name: Snorunt
d.flavorText: It feeds mainly on ice and snow. It's only able to survive in a limited number of places in the warm Alola region.

d.name: Froslass

attacks.name: Spiteful Sigh
attacks.text: Put up to 7 damage counters on this Pokémon. This attack does 20 damage for each damage counter you placed in this way.

attacks.name: Icy Wind
attacks.text: Your opponent's Active Pokémon is now Asleep.

d.flavorText: It freezes hikers who have come to climb snowy mountains and carries them back to its home. It only goes after men it thinks are handsome.

d.name: Finneon
d.flavorText: When night falls, their pink patterns begin to shine. They're popular with divers, so there are resorts that feed them to keep them close.

d.name: Lumineon

attacks.name: Neon Trickery
attacks.text: You may move an Energy from your opponent's Active Pokémon to 1 of their Benched Pokémon.

d.flavorText: Deep down at the bottom of the ocean, prey is scarce. Lumineon get into fierce disputes with Lanturn over food.

d.name: Snover

attacks.name: Powder Snow
attacks.text: Your opponent's Active Pokémon is now Asleep.

d.name: Tirtouga
d.flavorText: It was restored from an ancient fossil. Tirtouga lived in the sea but came up onto the land to search for prey.

d.name: Carracosta

attacks.name: Aqua Impact
attacks.text: This attack does 20 more damage for each Colorless in your opponent's Active Pokémon's Retreat Cost.

d.flavorText: Its jaws are terrifyingly powerful. It could eat Omastar and Omanyte whole and not be bothered in the slightest by their shells.

d.name: Cryogonal

attacks.name: Frozen Lock
attacks.text: Your opponent can't play any Item cards from their hand during their next turn.

d.flavorText: They are born in snow clouds. They use chains made of ice crystals to capture prey.

d.name: Keldeo-GX
rules: Pokémon-GX rule: When your Pokémon-GX is Knocked Out, your opponent takes 2 Prize cards.

abilities.name: Pure Heart
abilities.text: Prevent all effects of attacks, including damage, done to this Pokémon by your opponent's Pokémon-GX or Pokémon-EX.

attacks.name: Sonic Edge
attacks.text: This attack's damage isn't affected by any effects on your opponent's Active Pokémon.

attacks.name: Resolute Blade-GX
attacks.text: This attack does 50 damage for each of your opponent's Benched Pokémon. (You can't use more than 1 GX attack in a game.)

d.name: Dewpider
d.flavorText: When two Dewpider meet, they display their water bubbles to each other. Then the one with the smaller bubble gets out of the other's way.

d.name: Araquanid

attacks.name: Tangle Drag
attacks.text: Switch 1 of your opponent's Benched Pokémon with their Active Pokémon.

attacks.name: Sticky Web
attacks.text: During your opponent's next turn, the Defending Pokémon's attacks cost Colorless more, and its Retreat Cost is Colorless more.

d.flavorText: It usually passes its time in the water. When its belly is full, it stores its subdued prey in the water bubble on its head.

d.name: Wimpod

attacks.name: Sand Attack
attacks.text: If the Defending Pokémon tries to attack during your opponent's next turn, your opponent flips a coin. If tails, that attack doesn't happen.

d.flavorText: It will pick up anything it finds on the ground. Sometimes it finds coins, so Murkrow and Meowth will go after it.

d.name: Golisopod

abilities.name: Emergency Exit
abilities.text: If this Pokémon has 2 or fewer Energy attached to it, it has no Retreat Cost.

attacks.name: First Impression
attacks.text: If this Pokémon was on the Bench and became your Active Pokémon this turn, this attack does 60 more damage.

d.flavorText: The shell covering its body is as hard as diamond. This Pokémon will do anything it takes to win.

d.name: Pyukumuku

attacks.name: Collect
attacks.text: Draw a card.

d.flavorText: The tradition known as Pyukumuku chucking started from the custom of throwing Pyukumuku back into the sea after they wash onshore.

d.name: Tapu Fini

attacks.name: Nature Wave
attacks.text: If your opponent has any Ultra Beasts in play, this attack can be used for Colorless.

d.flavorText: This guardian deity of Poni Island manipulates water. Because it lives deep within a thick fog, it came to be both feared and revered.

d.name: Raichu & Alolan Raichu-GX
rules: TAG TEAM rule: When your TAG TEAM is Knocked Out, your opponent takes 3 Prize cards.

attacks.name: Tandem Shock
attacks.text: If this Pokémon was on the Bench and became your Active Pokémon this turn, this attack does 80 more damage, and your opponent's Active Pokémon is now Paralyzed.

attacks.name: Lightning Ride-GX
attacks.text: Switch this Pokémon with 1 of your Benched Pokémon. If this Pokémon has at least 2 extra Lightning Energy attached to it (in addition to this attack's cost), this attack does 100 more damage. (You can't use more than 1 GX attack in a game.)

d.name: Pikachu

attacks.name: Meal Time
attacks.text: Flip a coin until you get tails. For each heads, draw a card.

d.flavorText: Its nature is to store up electricity. Forests where nests of Pikachu live are dangerous, since the trees are so often struck by lightning.

d.name: Pikachu
d.flavorText: Its nature is to store up electricity. Forests where nests of Pikachu live are dangerous, since the trees are so often struck by lightning.

d.name: Alolan Raichu

attacks.name: Electro Rain
attacks.text: Discard any amount of Lightning Energy from this Pokémon. Then, for each Energy you discarded in this way, choose 1 of your opponent's Pokémon and do 30 damage to it. (You can choose the same Pokémon more than once.) This damage isn't affected by Weakness or Resistance.

d.flavorText: It focuses psychic energy into its tail and rides it like it's surfing. Another name for this Pokémon is "hodad."

d.name: Magnemite

attacks.name: Supersonic
attacks.text: Your opponent's Active Pokémon is now Confused.

d.flavorText: It's frequently the cause of power outages, which is why some power plants send out electrical signals that it can't stand.

d.name: Magneton

attacks.name: Tri Attack
attacks.text: Flip 3 coins. This attack does 40 damage for each heads.

d.flavorText: Delicate equipment can malfunction in areas inhabited by Magneton, which send out mysterious electrical signals.

d.name: Magnezone

abilities.name: Double Type
abilities.text: As long as this Pokémon is in play, it is Lightning and Metal type.

attacks.name: Magnetic Bolt
attacks.text: Put a Trainer card from your discard pile into your hand.

d.flavorText: It uses radar to monitor its territory. Intruders are quickly disposed of with a hyper beam.

d.name: Joltik

attacks.name: Jolt
attacks.text: Flip a coin. If heads, your opponent's Active Pokémon is now Paralyzed.

d.flavorText: Since it can't generate its own electricity, it sticks onto large-bodied Pokémon and absorbs static electricity.

d.name: Galvantula

attacks.name: Live Wire
attacks.text: This attack does 50 damage to 1 of your opponent's Pokémon. Also apply Weakness and Resistance for Benched Pokémon.

d.flavorText: They employ an electrically charged web to trap their prey. While it is immobilized by shock, they leisurely consume it.

d.name: Tynamo

attacks.name: Wild River
attacks.text: Switch this Pokémon with 1 of your Benched Pokémon.

d.flavorText: While one alone doesn't have much power, a chain of many Tynamo can be as powerful as lightning.

d.name: Tynamo

attacks.name: Generate Electricity
attacks.text: Search your deck for a Lightning Energy card and attach it to this Pokémon. Then, shuffle your deck.

d.flavorText: While one alone doesn't have much power, a chain of many Tynamo can be as powerful as lightning.

d.name: Eelektrik

attacks.name: Overspark
attacks.text: Discard all Lightning Energy from this Pokémon. This attack does 30 damage for each card you discarded in this way.

d.flavorText: It wraps itself around its prey and paralyzes it with electricity from the round spots on its sides. Then it chomps.

d.name: Eelektross

abilities.name: Electric Swamp
abilities.text: Once during your turn (before your attack), if this Pokémon is in your hand and you have at least 4 Lightning Energy cards in play, you may play this Pokémon onto your Bench. If you do, move any number of Lightning Energy from your other Pokémon to this Pokémon.

attacks.name: Hover Over
attacks.text: The Defending Pokémon can't retreat during your opponent's next turn.

d.flavorText: With their sucker mouths, they suck in prey. Then they use their fangs to shock the prey with electricity.

d.name: Stunfisk

attacks.name: Trap Bolt
attacks.text: If, before doing damage, your opponent's Active Pokémon has more remaining HP than this Pokémon, this attack does 30 more damage.

d.flavorText: Its skin is very hard, so it is unhurt even if stepped on by sumo wrestlers. It smiles when transmitting electricity.

d.name: Thundurus

attacks.name: Thunderous Gale
attacks.text: If Tornadus is on your Bench, this attack does 50 more damage.

attacks.name: Raging Thunder
attacks.text: This attack does 40 damage to 1 of your Benched Pokémon. (Don't apply Weakness and Resistance for Benched Pokémon.)

d.flavorText: The spikes on its tail discharge immense bolts of lightning. It flies around the Unova region firing off lightning bolts.

d.name: Tapu Koko

attacks.name: Nature Dive
attacks.text: If your opponent's Active Pokémon is an Ultra Beast, this attack does 100 more damage, and discard 2 Energy from this Pokémon.

d.flavorText: Although it's called a guardian deity, if a person or Pokémon puts it in a bad mood, it will become a malevolent deity and attack.

d.name: Xurkitree

attacks.name: Three Mirrors
attacks.text: If your opponent has exactly 3 Prize cards remaining, this attack does 90 more damage.

attacks.name: Signal Beam
attacks.text: Your opponent's Active Pokémon is now Confused.

d.flavorText: Although it's alien to this world and a danger here, it's apparently a common organism in the world where it normally lives.

d.name: Mewtwo & Mew-GX
rules: TAG TEAM rule: When your TAG TEAM is Knocked Out, your opponent takes 3 Prize cards.

abilities.name: Perfection
abilities.text: This Pokémon can use the attacks of any Pokémon-GX or Pokémon-EX on your Bench or in your discard pile. (You still need the necessary Energy to use each attack.)

attacks.name: Miraculous Duo-GX
attacks.text: If this Pokémon has at least 1 extra Energy attached to it (in addition to this attack's cost), heal all damage from all of your Pokémon. (You can't use more than 1 GX attack in a game.)

d.name: Espeon & Deoxys-GX
rules: TAG TEAM rule: When your TAG TEAM is Knocked Out, your opponent takes 3 Prize cards.

attacks.name: Psychic Club
attacks.text: This attack does 30 more damage for each of your Benched Psychic Pokémon.

attacks.name: Cross Division-GX
attacks.text: Put 10 damage counters on your opponent's Pokémon in any way you like. If this Pokémon has at least 3 extra Energy attached to it (in addition to this attack's cost), put 20 damage counters on them instead. (You can't use more than 1 GX attack in a game.)

d.name: Exeggcute

attacks.name: Leech Seed
attacks.text: Heal 10 damage from this Pokémon.

d.flavorText: Six of them form a single Pokémon. Should one of the six be lost, the next morning there will once more be six.

d.name: Exeggutor

attacks.name: Mind Bend
attacks.text: Your opponent's Active Pokémon is now Confused.

attacks.name: Full Clean
attacks.text: Discard your hand.

d.flavorText: It engages its enemies using psychic powers. Each of its three heads fires off psychokinetic energy, tripling its power.

d.name: Alolan Marowak

attacks.name: Spirit Smash
attacks.text: Discard the top card of your opponent's deck. If the card you discarded is a Pokémon, this attack does damage equal to that Pokémon's HP to your opponent's Active Pokémon.

d.flavorText: The rich greenery of the Alola region is hard on Marowak. It controls fire to stay alive.

d.name: Jynx

abilities.name: Ominous Posture
abilities.text: Once during your turn (before your attack), you may move 1 damage counter from 1 of your Pokémon to another of your Pokémon.

attacks.name: Attract Smack
attacks.text: Flip a coin. If heads, your opponent's Active Pokémon is now Paralyzed.

d.flavorText: It sways its hips to a rhythm all its own. The precise movements of Jynx living in Alola are truly wonderful.

d.name: Wynaut

abilities.name: Peppy Pick
abilities.text: Once during your turn (before your attack), you may flip a coin. If heads, choose a random card from your opponent's hand. Your opponent reveals that card and shuffles it into their deck. If you use this Ability, your turn ends.

d.flavorText: It tends to move in a pack with others. They cluster in a tight group to sleep in a cave.

d.name: Latios-GX
rules: Pokémon-GX rule: When your Pokémon-GX is Knocked Out, your opponent takes 2 Prize cards.

abilities.name: Power Bind
abilities.text: If you have 4 or fewer Pokémon in play, this Pokémon can't attack.

attacks.name: Tag Purge
attacks.text: During your opponent's next turn, prevent all damage done to this Pokémon by attacks from TAG TEAM Pokémon.

attacks.name: Clear Vision-GX
attacks.text: For the rest of this game, your opponent can't use any GX attacks. (You can't use more than 1 GX attack in a game.)

d.name: Jirachi-GX
rules: Pokémon-GX rule: When your Pokémon-GX is Knocked Out, your opponent takes 2 Prize cards.

abilities.name: Psychic Zone
abilities.text: Don't apply Psychic Weakness when Pokémon (both yours and your opponent's) take damage from attacks.

attacks.name: Star Search
attacks.text: Search your deck for an Energy card and attach it to 1 of your Psychic Pokémon. Then, shuffle your deck.

attacks.name: Star Shield-GX
attacks.text: Prevent all effects of attacks, including damage, done to this Pokémon during your opponent's next turn. (You can't use more than 1 GX attack in a game.)

d.name: Drifloon
d.flavorText: Its round body is stuffed with souls and expands each time it leads someone away.

d.name: Drifblim

abilities.name: Tag Transport
abilities.text: Once during your turn (before your attack), you may switch your Active TAG TEAM Pokémon with 1 of your Benched Pokémon.

d.flavorText: There's a rumor that if you catch a Drifblim floating on the wind at dusk, you'll be carried away to the afterlife.

d.name: Skorupi

attacks.name: Knock Off
attacks.text: Discard a random card from your opponent's hand.

d.flavorText: It grips prey with its tail claws and injects poison. It tenaciously hangs on until the poison takes.

d.name: Uxie

abilities.name: Secret Territory
abilities.text: If you have Mesprit and Azelf in play, apply Weakness for each Pokémon (both yours and your opponent's) as ×4 instead.

d.flavorText: Known as "The Being of Knowledge." It is said that it can wipe out the memory of those who see its eyes.

d.name: Mesprit

attacks.name: First Contact
attacks.text: Search your deck for up to 3 Basic Pokémon and put them onto your Bench. Then, shuffle your deck.

d.flavorText: Known as "The Being of Emotion." It taught humans the nobility of sorrow, pain, and joy.

d.name: Azelf

attacks.name: Psypower
attacks.text: Put 3 damage counters on your opponent's Pokémon in any way you like.

d.flavorText: Known as "The Being of Willpower." It sleeps at the bottom of a lake to keep the world in balance.

d.name: Giratina

abilities.name: Dimension Breach
abilities.text: When you play this Pokémon from your hand onto your Bench during your turn, you may discard a Special Energy from your opponent's Active Pokémon.

attacks.name: Fade to Black
attacks.text: Your opponent's Active Pokémon is now Confused.

d.flavorText: This Pokémon is said to live in a world on the reverse side of ours, where common knowledge is distorted and strange.

d.name: Cresselia

attacks.name: Aurora Gain
attacks.text: Heal 30 damage from this Pokémon.

attacks.name: Luminous Blade
attacks.text: Discard a Psychic Energy from this Pokémon.

d.flavorText: Shiny particles are released from its wings like a veil. It is said to represent the crescent moon.

d.name: Munna

attacks.name: Future Sight
attacks.text: Look at the top 4 cards of either player's deck and put them back in any order.

d.flavorText: This Pokémon appears before people and Pokémon who are having nightmares and eats those dreams.

d.name: Musharna

attacks.name: Rest Well
attacks.text: Both Active Pokémon are now Asleep. During your next turn, this Pokémon's attacks do 100 more damage to your opponent's Active Pokémon (before applying Weakness and Resistance).

d.flavorText: The mist emanating from their foreheads is packed with the dreams of people and Pokémon.

d.name: Elgyem

attacks.name: Psybeam
attacks.text: Your opponent's Active Pokémon is now Confused.

d.flavorText: It controls tremendous psychic power. Most reports of alien sightings are actually just people mistaking Elgyem for an alien.

d.name: Beheeyem

attacks.name: Mysterious Noise
attacks.text: Shuffle this Pokémon and all cards attached to it into your deck. Your opponent can't play any Item cards from their hand during their next turn.

d.flavorText: With its psychic powers, it rewrites its opponents' memories. You, too, may have already had your memories rewritten.

d.name: Honedge

attacks.name: Lucky Find
attacks.text: Search your deck for an Item card, reveal it, and put it into your hand. Then, shuffle your deck.

d.flavorText: Apparently this Pokémon is born when a departed spirit inhabits a sword. It attaches itself to people and drinks their life force.

d.name: Honedge

attacks.name: Slashing Cutter
attacks.text: This attack's damage isn't affected by Weakness or Resistance.

d.flavorText: Apparently this Pokémon is born when a departed spirit inhabits a sword. It attaches itself to people and drinks their life force.

d.name: Doublade

attacks.name: Slashing Cutter
attacks.text: This attack's damage isn't affected by Weakness or Resistance.

d.flavorText: When Honedge evolves, it divides into two swords, which cooperate via telepathy to coordinate attacks and slash their enemies to ribbons.

d.name: Aegislash

abilities.name: Durable Blade
abilities.text: If this Pokémon is Knocked Out by damage from an opponent's attack, put it into your hand instead of the discard pile. (Discard all cards attached to it.)

attacks.name: Trash Slash
attacks.text: This attack does 10 damage for each Item card in your discard pile. You can't do more than 130 damage in this way.

d.flavorText: Generations of kings were attended by these Pokémon, which used their spectral power to manipulate and control people and Pokémon.

d.name: Mareanie
d.flavorText: They eat Corsola branches, so Mareanie are hated by craftsmen who work with Corsola branches that have naturally fallen off.

d.name: Toxapex
d.flavorText: To attack, this Pokémon sends toxic spikes flying at its enemies. Ones that come close get mown down by the claws on its feet.

d.name: Salandit
d.flavorText: The males will do whatever the females tell them. They give the females most of their food. Due to malnutrition, the males can't evolve.

d.name: Salazzle
d.flavorText: Salazzle lives deep in caves and forces the Salandit it has attracted with its pheromones to serve it.

d.name: Cosmog
d.flavorText: Even though its helpless, gaseous body can be blown away by the slightest breeze, it doesn't seem to care.

d.name: Necrozma

attacks.name: Barrier Attack
attacks.text: During your opponent's next turn, this Pokémon takes 30 less damage from attacks (after applying Weakness and Resistance).

attacks.name: Special Laser
attacks.text: If this Pokémon has any Special Energy attached to it, this attack does 60 more damage.

d.flavorText: It looks somehow pained as it rages around in search of light, which serves as its energy. It's apparently from another world.

d.name: Poipole

attacks.name: Last Scene
attacks.text: If each player has exactly 1 Prize card remaining, this attack does 130 more damage.

d.flavorText: This Ultra Beast is well enough liked to be chosen as a first partner in its own world.

d.name: Onix

attacks.name: Bedrock Press
attacks.text: During your opponent's next turn, this Pokémon takes 20 less damage from attacks (after applying Weakness and Resistance).

d.flavorText: Burrows at high speed in search of food. The tunnels it leaves are used as homes by Diglett.

d.name: Steelix

attacks.name: Ground Stream
attacks.text: Attach 2 Fighting Energy cards from your discard pile to this Pokémon.

attacks.name: Gigaton Shake
attacks.text: During your next turn, your Pokémon can't attack. (This includes Pokémon that come into play on that turn.)

d.flavorText: Tempered underground under high pressure and heat, its body is harder than any metal.

d.name: Cubone

attacks.name: Growl
attacks.text: During your opponent's next turn, the Defending Pokémon's attacks do 20 less damage (before applying Weakness and Resistance).

attacks.name: Bonemerang
attacks.text: Flip 2 coins. This attack does 20 damage for each heads.

d.flavorText: At night, it weeps loudly for its dead mother, but those cries only attract its natural enemy—Mandibuzz.

d.name: Aerodactyl-GX
rules: Pokémon-GX rule: When your Pokémon-GX is Knocked Out, your opponent takes 2 Prize cards.

abilities.name: Primal Winds
abilities.text: As long as this Pokémon is your Active Pokémon, your opponent's Basic Pokémon's attacks cost Colorless more.

attacks.name: Wild Dive-GX
attacks.text: This attack does 50 damage times the amount of Energy attached to your opponent's Active Pokémon. (You can't use more than 1 GX attack in a game.)

d.name: Heracross

attacks.name: Turn the Tables
attacks.text: If 1 of your opponent's Pokémon used a GX attack during their last turn, your opponent shuffles their Active Pokémon and all cards attached to it into their deck.

d.flavorText: It's proud of its thick horn. In Alola, its biggest rival is Vikavolt, which it's always fighting with.

d.name: Breloom

attacks.name: Spore
attacks.text: Your opponent's Active Pokémon is now Asleep.

attacks.name: Pre-Dawn Strike
attacks.text: If your opponent's Active Pokémon is Asleep, this attack does 90 more damage.

d.flavorText: Its short arms stretch when it throws punches. Its technique is equal to that of pro boxers.

d.name: Meditite

attacks.name: Spirited Headbutt
attacks.text: This Pokémon can't use Spirited Headbutt during your next turn.

d.flavorText: It always trains deep in mountains. It levitates when it heightens its spiritual power through meditation.

d.name: Medicham

attacks.name: Pure Power
attacks.text: Put 4 damage counters on your opponent's Pokémon in any way you like.

attacks.name: Master Strike
attacks.text: If this Pokémon has a Karate Belt card attached to it, this attack does 60 more damage.

d.flavorText: It elegantly avoids attacks with dance-like steps, then launches a devastating blow in the same motion.

d.name: Relicanth

attacks.name: Deep Sea Boring
attacks.text: Search your deck for a Trainer card, reveal it, and put it into your hand. Then, shuffle your deck.

attacks.name: Water Pulse
attacks.text: Your opponent's Active Pokémon is now Asleep.

d.flavorText: Thought to have gone extinct, Relicanth was given a name that is a variation of the name of the person who discovered it.

d.name: Gible
d.flavorText: It reacts to anything that moves—flies right at it and bites it. Sometimes it injures itself, but it doesn't care too much.

d.name: Gabite
d.flavorText: It loves shiny things. When it finds a Sableye trying to catch a Carbink, Gabite becomes furiously angry and attacks the Sableye.

d.name: Garchomp

abilities.name: Avenging Aura
abilities.text: If you have more Prize cards remaining than your opponent, this Pokémon's attacks do 80 more damage to your opponent's Active Pokémon (before applying Weakness and Resistance).

attacks.name: Over Slice
attacks.text: You may discard an Energy from this Pokémon. If you do, this attack does 40 more damage.

d.flavorText: It flies at the speed of sound while searching for prey, and it has midair battles with Salamence as the two compete for food.

d.name: Riolu
d.flavorText: It knows how people and Pokémon feel by looking at their auras. It doesn't approach dangerous opponents.

d.name: Riolu
d.flavorText: It knows how people and Pokémon feel by looking at their auras. It doesn't approach dangerous opponents.

d.name: Lucario

abilities.name: Tag Coach
abilities.text: Your TAG TEAM Pokémon take 20 less damage from your opponent's attacks (after applying Weakness and Resistance).

d.flavorText: It concentrates its mental energy and fires off mysterious waves called auras, which can crush boulders of large size to dust.

d.name: Drilbur
d.flavorText: It makes its way swiftly through the soil by putting both claws together and rotating at high speed.

d.name: Excadrill

attacks.name: Rototiller
attacks.text: Shuffle 4 cards from your discard pile into your deck.

d.flavorText: It can help in tunnel construction. Its drill has evolved into steel strong enough to bore through iron plates.

d.name: Archen

attacks.name: Endeavor
attacks.text: Flip 2 coins. This attack does 20 more damage for each heads.

d.flavorText: Once thought to be the ancestor of all bird Pokémon, some of the latest research suggests that may not be the case.

d.name: Archeops

attacks.name: U-turn
attacks.text: Switch this Pokémon with 1 of your Benched Pokémon.

attacks.name: Hyper Beam
attacks.text: Discard an Energy from your opponent's Active Pokémon.

d.flavorText: This ancient Pokémon's plumage is delicate, so if anyone other than an experienced professional tries to restore it, they will fail.

d.name: Terrakion

attacks.name: Cavern Counter
attacks.text: If all of your Benched Pokémon have at least 1 damage counter on them, this attack does 150 more damage.

d.flavorText: Its charge is strong enough to break through a giant castle wall in one blow. This Pokémon is spoken of in legends.

d.name: Meloetta

attacks.name: Tag Cheer
attacks.text: Attach an Energy card from your hand to 1 of your TAG TEAM Pokémon.

attacks.name: Shooting Star Pirouette
attacks.text: Flip a coin until you get tails. This attack does 30 more damage for each heads.

d.flavorText: The melodies sung by Meloetta have the power to make Pokémon that hear them happy or sad.

d.name: Zygarde

abilities.name: Cellular Companions
abilities.text: As long as this Pokémon is on your Bench, your Zygarde's and Zygarde-GX's attacks do 20 more damage to your opponent's Active Pokémon (before applying Weakness and Resistance).

attacks.name: Boost Fang
attacks.text: Attach a Fighting Energy card from your discard pile to 1 of your Benched Pokémon.

d.flavorText: This is Zygarde when about 10% of its pieces have been assembled. It leaps at its opponent's chest and sinks its sharp fangs into them.

d.name: Umbreon & Darkrai-GX
rules: TAG TEAM rule: When your TAG TEAM is Knocked Out, your opponent takes 3 Prize cards.

attacks.name: Black Lance
attacks.text: This attack does 60 damage to 1 of your opponent's Benched Pokémon-GX or Benched Pokémon-EX. (Don't apply Weakness and Resistance for Benched Pokémon.)

attacks.name: Dark Moon-GX
attacks.text: Your opponent can't play any Trainer cards from their hand during their next turn. If this Pokémon has at least 5 extra Darkness Energy attached to it (in addition to this attack's cost), your opponent's Active Pokémon is Knocked Out. (You can't use more than 1 GX attack in a game.)

d.name: Mega Sableye & Tyranitar-GX
rules: TAG TEAM rule: When your TAG TEAM is Knocked Out, your opponent takes 3 Prize cards.

attacks.name: Greedy Crush
attacks.text: If your opponent's Pokémon-GX or Pokémon-EX is Knocked Out by damage from this attack, take 1 more Prize card.

attacks.name: Gigafall-GX
attacks.text: If this Pokémon has at least 5 extra Energy attached to it (in addition to this attack's cost), discard the top 15 cards of your opponent's deck. (You can't use more than 1 GX attack in a game.)

d.name: Alolan Grimer

attacks.name: Collect
attacks.text: Draw 2 cards.

d.flavorText: There are a hundred or so of them living in Alola's waste-disposal site. They're all hard workers who eat a lot of trash.

d.name: Murkrow

attacks.name: Astonish
attacks.text: Choose a random card from your opponent's hand. Your opponent reveals that card and shuffles it into their deck.

d.flavorText: It has a weakness for shiny things. It's been known to sneak into the nests of Gabite—noted collectors of jewels—in search of treasure.

d.name: Murkrow
d.flavorText: It has a weakness for shiny things. It's been known to sneak into the nests of Gabite—noted collectors of jewels—in search of treasure.

d.name: Honchkrow

attacks.name: Sharpshooting
attacks.text: This attack does 30 damage to 1 of your opponent's Pokémon. (Don't apply Weakness and Resistance for Benched Pokémon.)

d.flavorText: It will absolutely not forgive failure from or betrayal by its goons. It has no choice in this if it wants to maintain the order of the flock.

d.name: Sneasel
d.flavorText: They will cooperate to steal eggs from the nests of bird Pokémon, but fights break out to determine which one gets to eat the eggs.

d.name: Weavile-GX
rules: Pokémon-GX rule: When your Pokémon-GX is Knocked Out, your opponent takes 2 Prize cards.

abilities.name: Shadow Connection
abilities.text: As often as you like during your turn (before your attack), you may move a basic Darkness Energy from 1 of your Pokémon to another of your Pokémon.

attacks.name: Nocturnal Maneuvers-GX
attacks.text: Search your deck for any number of Basic Pokémon and put them onto your Bench. Then, shuffle your deck. (You can't use more than 1 GX attack in a game.)

d.name: Sableye

attacks.name: Mirror Gem
attacks.text: During your opponent's next turn, if this Pokémon is damaged by an attack (even if it is Knocked Out), put 8 damage counters on the Attacking Pokémon.

d.flavorText: It digs through the ground with its hard claws and crunches down gems with its thick pointy teeth. Carbink is its favorite food.

d.name: Drapion

attacks.name: Cross Poison
attacks.text: Flip 4 coins. This attack does 50 damage for each heads. If at least 2 of them are heads, your opponent's Active Pokémon is now Poisoned.

d.flavorText: It takes pride in its strength. Even though it can tear foes apart, it finishes them off with powerful poison.

d.name: Purrloin

d.name: Liepard

d.name: Scrafty

d.flavorText: This Pokémon may be rude, but it takes very good care of its family, its friends, and its turf.

d.name: Yveltal

d.name: Hoopa

attacks.name: Evil Admonition

attacks.name: Mind Shock

d.flavorText: This troublemaker sends anything and everything to faraway places using its loop, which can warp space.

d.name: Kangaskhan

attacks.name: Double Draw

attacks.name: Tag Impact
attacks.text: This attack does 50 damage for each of your TAG TEAM Pokémon in play.

d.name: Tranquill

attacks.name: Air Slash
attacks.text: Discard an Energy from this Pokémon.

d.name: Yungoos

attacks.name: Alert Headbutt

d.name: Type: Null

attacks.name: Quick Blow

You may play as many Item cards as you like during your turn (before your attack).

attacks.name: Twin Play
attacks.text: Search your deck for up to 2 Scyther and put them onto your Bench. Then, shuffle your deck.

attacks.name: Agility
attacks.text: Flip a coin. If heads, prevent all effects of attacks, including damage, done to this Pokémon during your opponent's next turn.

d.flavorText: While young, they live together deep in the mountains, training themselves in how to fight with their scythes and move at high speeds.

d.name: Quagsire

abilities.name: Wash Out
abilities.text: As often as you like during your turn (before your attack), you may move a Water Energy from 1 of your Benched Pokémon to your Active Pokémon.

attacks.name: Hydro Pump
attacks.text: This attack does 20 more damage times the amount of Water Energy attached to this Pokémon.

d.flavorText: This carefree Pokémon has an easygoing nature. While swimming, it always bumps into boat hulls.

d.name: Froakie

abilities.name: Frubbles
abilities.text: If this Pokémon has any Water Energy attached to it, it has no Retreat Cost.

d.flavorText: It protects its skin by covering its body in delicate bubbles. Beneath its happy-go-lucky air, it keeps a watchful eye on its surroundings.

d.name: Frogadier

abilities.name: Gale Shuriken
abilities.text: When you play this Pokémon from your hand to evolve 1 of your Pokémon during your turn, you may put 2 damage counters on 1 of your opponent's Pokémon.

d.flavorText: Its swiftness is unparalleled. It can scale a tower of more than 2,000 feet in a minute's time.

d.name: Voltorb

abilities.name: Floating Electrons
abilities.text: If this Pokémon has any Energy attached to it, it has no Retreat Cost.

attacks.name: Thunder Shock
attacks.text: Flip a coin. If heads, your opponent's Active Pokémon is now Paralyzed.

d.flavorText: Usually found in power plants. Easily mistaken for a Poké Ball, it has zapped many people.

d.name: Xurkitree

attacks.name: Dazzle Blast
attacks.text: Your opponent's Active Pokémon is now Confused.

attacks.name: Cablegram
attacks.text: If you have exactly 3 Prize cards remaining, your opponent's Active Pokémon is now Paralyzed.

d.flavorText: It appeared from the Ultra Wormhole. It raided a power plant, so people think it energizes itself with electricity.

d.name: Seviper

abilities.name: More Poison
abilities.text: Put 1 more damage counter on your opponent's Poisoned Pokémon between turns.

attacks.name: Venomous Fang
attacks.text: Your opponent's Active Pokémon is now Poisoned.

d.flavorText: In battle, it uses its bladed tail to counter any Zangoose. It secretes a deadly venom in its tail.

d.name: Shuppet
d.flavorText: It loves vengeful emotions and hangs in rows under the eaves of houses where vengeful people live.

d.name: Inkay

attacks.name: Hypnosis
attacks.text: Your opponent's Active Pokémon is now Asleep.

d.flavorText: It flashes the light-emitting spots on its body, which drains its opponent's will to fight. It takes the opportunity to scuttle away and hide.

d.name: Malamar

abilities.name: Psychic Recharge
abilities.text: Once during your turn (before your attack), you may attach a Psychic Energy card from your discard pile to 1 of your Benched Pokémon.

d.flavorText: It lures prey close with hypnotic motions, then wraps its tentacles around it before finishing it off with digestive fluids.

d.name: Poipole

attacks.name: Spit Poison
attacks.text: Your opponent's Active Pokémon is now Poisoned.

attacks.name: Knockout Reviver
attacks.text: During your opponent's next turn, if this Pokémon is Knocked Out, your opponent can't take any Prize cards for it.

d.flavorText: This Ultra Beast is well enough liked to be chosen as a first partner in its own world.

d.name: Rowlet
d.flavorText: This wary Pokémon uses photosynthesis to store up energy during the day, while becoming active at night.

d.name: Sudowoodo

abilities.name: Roadblock
abilities.text: Your opponent can't have more than 4 Benched Pokémon. If they have 5 or more Benched Pokémon, they discard Benched Pokémon until they have 4 Pokémon on the Bench. If more than one effect changes the number of Benched Pokémon allowed, use the smaller number.

d.flavorText: To avoid attack, it mimics a tree. It will run off if splashed with water, which it hates.

d.name: Riolu

attacks.name: Detect
attacks.text: Flip a coin. If heads, prevent all effects of attacks, including damage, done to this Pokémon during your opponent's next turn.

d.flavorText: It's tough enough to run right through the night, and it's also a hard worker, but it's still just a youngster.

d.name: Lucario

abilities.name: Precognitive Aura
abilities.text: Once during your turn (before your attack), if you have Garchomp in play, you may search your deck for a card and put it into your hand. Then, shuffle your deck.

attacks.name: Missile Jab
attacks.text: This attack's damage isn't affected by Resistance.

d.flavorText: They can detect the species of a living being—and its emotions—from over half a mile away. They control auras and hunt their prey in packs.

d.name: Rockruff

attacks.name: Surprise Attack
attacks.text: Flip a coin. If tails, this attack does nothing.

d.flavorText: This Pokémon has lived with people since times long ago. It can sense when its Trainer is in the dumps and will stick close by its Trainer's side.

d.name: Buzzwole

attacks.name: Sledgehammer
attacks.text: If your opponent has exactly 4 Prize cards remaining, this attack does 90 more damage.

attacks.name: Swing Around
attacks.text: Flip 2 coins. This attack does 20 more damage for each heads.

d.flavorText: A mysterious life-form called an Ultra Beast. Witnesses saw it pulverize a dump truck with a single punch.

d.name: Zorua
d.flavorText: It changes so it looks like its foe, tricks it, and then uses that opportunity to flee.

d.name: Guzzlord

attacks.name: Lord's Valley
attacks.text: If you have exactly 2, 4, or 6 Prize cards remaining, discard the top 10 cards of your deck.

d.flavorText: A dangerous Ultra Beast, it appears to be eating constantly, but for some reason its droppings have never been found.

d.name: Magnemite

attacks.name: Searching Magnet
attacks.text: Search your deck for up to 3 Metal Energy cards, reveal them, and put them into your hand. Then, shuffle your deck.

d.flavorText: It sends out electromagnetic waves, which let it float through the air. Touching it while it's eating electricity will give you a full-body shock.

d.name: Magneton

attacks.name: Zap Cannon
attacks.text: This Pokémon can't use Zap Cannon during your next turn.

d.flavorText: It has about three times the electrical power of Magnemite. For some reason, outbreaks of this Pokémon happen when lots of sunspots appear.

d.name: Magnezone

abilities.name: Magnetic Circuit
abilities.text: As often as you like during your turn (before your attack), you may attach a Metal Energy card from your hand to 1 of your Pokémon.

attacks.name: Zap Cannon
attacks.text: This Pokémon can't use Zap Cannon during your next turn.

d.flavorText: As it zooms through the sky, this Pokémon seems to be receiving signals of unknown origin, while transmitting signals of unknown purpose.

d.name: Dartrix

attacks.name: Sharp Blade Quill
attacks.text: This attack does 20 damage to 1 of your opponent's Pokémon. (Don't apply Weakness and Resistance for Benched Pokémon.)

attacks.name: Leaf Blade
attacks.text: Flip a coin. If heads, this attack does 20 more damage.

d.flavorText: A bit of a dandy, it spends its free time preening its wings. Its preoccupation with any dirt on its plumage can leave it unable to battle.

d.name: Beldum

attacks.name: Core Beam
attacks.text: Discard a Metal Energy from this Pokémon.

d.flavorText: Its cells are all magnets. It uses magnetism to communicate with others of its kind.

d.name: Metang

attacks.name: Core Beam
attacks.text: Discard a Metal Energy from this Pokémon.

d.flavorText: When two Beldum link together, their psychic power is doubled. Their intelligence, however, remains unchanged.

d.name: Celesteela

attacks.name: Moon Raker
attacks.text: If the total of both players' remaining Prize cards is exactly 6, this attack can be used for Metal.

d.flavorText: One kind of Ultra Beast. Witnesses have seen it burn down a forest by expelling gas from its two arms.

d.name: Kartana

attacks.name: Divine Paper
attacks.text: If your opponent has exactly 6 Prize cards remaining, this attack does 90 more damage.

d.flavorText: One of the Ultra Beast life-forms, it was observed cutting down a gigantic steel tower with one stroke of its blade.

d.name: Ralts

attacks.name: Draining Kiss
attacks.text: Heal 10 damage from this Pokémon.

d.flavorText: If its horns capture the warm feelings of people or Pokémon, its body warms up slightly.

d.name: Kirlia
d.flavorText: The cheerful spirit of its Trainer gives it energy for its psychokinetic power. It spins and dances when happy.

d.name: Diancie

attacks.name: Sparkling Wish
attacks.text: Search your deck for a card that evolves from 1 of your Pokémon and put it onto that Pokémon to evolve it. Then, shuffle your deck.

attacks.name: Diamond Storm
attacks.text: Heal 30 damage from each of your Fairy Pokémon.

d.flavorText: A sudden transformation of Carbink, its pink, glimmering body is said to be the loveliest sight in the whole world.

d.name: Altaria

abilities.name: Fight Song
abilities.text: Your Dragon Pokémon's attacks do 20 more damage to your opponent's Active Pokémon (before applying Weakness and Resistance).

d.flavorText: On sunny days, it flies freely through the sky and blends into the clouds. It sings in a beautiful soprano.

d.name: Gible

attacks.name: Ascension
attacks.text: Search your deck for a card that evolves from this Pokémon and put it onto this Pokémon to evolve it. Then, shuffle your deck.

d.flavorText: It skulks in caves, and when prey or an enemy passes by, it leaps out and chomps them. The force of its attack sometimes chips its teeth.

d.name: Gabite

attacks.name: Ascension
attacks.text: Search your deck for a card that evolves from this Pokémon and put it onto this Pokémon to evolve it. Then, shuffle your deck.

d.flavorText: Shiny objects are its passion. It can be found in its cave, scarcely moving, its gaze fixed on the jewels it's amassed or Carbink it has caught.

d.name: Wimpod

abilities.name: Wimp Out
abilities.text: During your first turn, this Pokémon has no Retreat Cost.

d.name: Slowpoke

d.name: Staryu

d.name: Magikarp
d.flavorText: In the distant past, they were fairly strong, but they have become gradually weaker over time.

d.name: Gyarados-GX

attacks.name: Hyper Beam-GX
attacks.text: (You can't use more than 1 GX attack in a game.)

d.name: Lapras

d.name: Vaporeon

attacks.name: Bubble Drain
attacks.text: Heal 30 damage from this Pokémon.

d.flavorText: Clean, clear waters are its usual habitat. When it's about to be attacked by an invading enemy, it dives into the water to hide.

d.name: Pikachu
d.flavorText: Its nature is to store up electricity. Forests where nests of Pikachu live are dangerous, since the trees are so often struck by lightning.

d.name: Raichu-GX
rules: Pokémon-GX rule: When your Pokémon-GX is Knocked Out, your opponent takes 2 Prize cards.

attacks.name: Spark Ball-GX
attacks.text: (You can't use more than 1 GX attack in a game.)

d.name: Voltorb
d.flavorText: It was discovered when Poké Balls were introduced. It is said that there is some connection.

d.name: Electrode

attacks.name: Electroblast
attacks.text: Flip 2 coins. This attack does 30 more damage for each heads.

d.flavorText: It explodes in response to even minor stimuli. It is feared, with the nickname of "The Bomb Ball."

d.name: Jolteon

abilities.name: Electromagnetic Wall

d.flavorText: Its lungs contain an organ that creates electricity. The crackling sound of electricity can be heard when it exhales.

d.name: Zapdos

attacks.name: Hurricane Call

d.flavorText: A legendary bird Pokémon that is said to appear from clouds while dropping enormous lightning bolts.

d.name: Ekans

attacks.name: Wrap

d.flavorText: By dislocating its jaw, it can swallow prey larger than itself. After a meal, it curls up and rests.

d.flavorText: The latest research has determined that there are over 20 possible arrangements of the patterns on its stomach.

d.name: Koffing
d.flavorText: Its thin, balloon-like body is inflated by horribly toxic gases. It reeks when it is nearby.

d.name: Weezing

d.flavorText: If one of the twin Koffing inflates, the other one deflates. It constantly mixes its poisonous gases.

d.name: Jynx
d.flavorText: It sways its hips to a rhythm all its own. The precise movements of Jynx living in Alola are truly wonderful.

d.name: Mewtwo-GX
rules: Pokémon-GX rule: When your Pokémon-GX is Knocked Out, your opponent takes 2 Prize cards.

attacks.name: Psycrush-GX
attacks.text: Discard all Energy from your opponent's Active Pokémon. (You can't use more than 1 GX attack in a game.)

d.name: Mew
d.flavorText: Because it can use all kinds of moves, many scientists believe Mew to be the ancestor of Pokémon.

d.name: Geodude
d.flavorText: Geodude that have lived a long life have had all their edges smoothed out until they're totally round. They also have a calm, quiet disposition.

d.name: Graveler

attacks.name: Mudslide

d.flavorText: It climbs up cliffs as it heads toward the peak of a mountain. As soon as it reaches the summit, it rolls back down the way it came.

d.name: Golem

attacks.name: Rock Slide
attacks.text: This attack does 20 damage to 3 of your opponent's Benched Pokémon. (Don't apply Weakness and Resistance for Benched Pokémon.)

d.flavorText: When Golem grow old, they stop shedding their shells. Those that have lived a long, long time have shells green with moss.

d.name: Onix-GX

attacks.text: Flip a coin. If heads, your opponent's Active Pokémon is now Paralyzed.

d.name: Cubone

attacks.name: Sharpshooting

d.name: Clefairy

d.name: Clefairy
d.flavorText: They're popular, but they're rare. Trainers who show them off recklessly may be targeted by thieves.

d.name: Clefable
d.flavorText: It can't help but hear a pin drop from over half a mile away, so it lives deep in the mountains where there aren't many people or Pokémon.

d.name: Jigglypuff
d.flavorText: Recordings of Jigglypuff's strange lullabies can be purchased from department stores. These CDs can be found near the bedding area.

attacks.text: Heal all damage from this Pokémon. (You can't use more than 1 GX attack in a game.)

attacks.name: Double Slap

d.flavorText: Its pantomime skills are wonderful. You may become enraptured while watching it, but next thing you know, Mr. Mime has made a real wall.

(Don't apply Weakness and Resistance for Benched Pokémon.) (You can't use more than 1 GX attack in a game.)

d.name: Farfetch'd
d.flavorText: The plant stalk it holds is its weapon. The stalk is used like a sword to cut all sorts of things.

attacks.name: Double-Edge
attacks.text: This Pokémon does 20 damage to itself.

d.flavorText: It seems that other Pokémon's efforts to take its delicious, nutritious egg away from it caused Chansey to get faster at fleeing.

d.name: Kangaskhan

d.name: Snorlax

attacks.text: Discard an Energy from this Pokémon.

attacks.text: This attack does 10 more damage times the amount of Water Energy attached to this Pokémon.

d.name: Pikachu

attacks.name: Iron Tail
attacks.text: Flip a coin until you get tails. This attack does 20 damage for each heads.

d.flavorText: A plan was recently announced to gather many Pikachu and make an electric power plant.

attacks.text: Heal 30 damage from this Pokémon.
